_comment: The original command behind each ctools command and the version ctools is pinned to.
scripts/sync_attribution.py copies this file into docs/ATTRIBUTION.md, the Acknowledgments section of each help
file in build/, help ctools, and the *! original: lines of the ado-files. After editing, run:
new_commands lists the ctools commands that reimplement no Stata command (csql), with the software they build on.
Text fields use a small markup: `command`, *italic*, **bold**, [text](url).

stata.full: StataNow/MP 19.5 for Windows (64-bit x86-64), revision 14 Oct 2026

commands.intro: `cdistinct` reimplements `distinct`, written by Gary Longton (Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center) and Nicholas J. Cox (Durham University). Its syntax, options, output, and stored results follow `distinct`.

originals.name: distinct
originals.authors: Gary Longton and Nicholas J. Cox
originals.note: This is the date of the package file in the *Stata Journal* software archive. The package does not state a distribution date. SSC distributes an older version, 1.2.1 (March 1, 2012).

later: SSC distributes an older version of `distinct`, 1.2.1 (March 1, 2012). The authors have since published four versions in the *Stata Journal*: 1.3.0 (July 22, 2015; dm0042_2, 15(3)), 1.4.1 (October 10, 2020; dm0042_3, 20(4)), 1.4.2 (August 15, 2022; dm0042_4, 23(2)), and 1.4.3 (September 3, 2023; dm0042_5, 23(4)). `cdistinct` follows 1.4.3. Compared with the SSC copy, it displays a different table, uses different defaults for `abbrev()` and `minimum()`, and accepts `sort()` and `width()`. `search dm0042, entry` lists the *Stata Journal* versions. The same package contains the companion command `distinctgen`. ctools does not reimplement `distinctgen`.
credits: According to its help file, `distinct` grew out of a program that Patrick Royston posted to Statalist.
references: Cox, N. J., and G. M. Longton. 2008. Speaking Stata: Distinct observations. *Stata Journal* 8(4): 557-568.

Longton, G., and N. J. Cox. 2002. DISTINCT: Stata module to display distinct values of variables. Statistical Software Components S424201, Boston College Department of Economics. Revised March 21, 2012.

commands.intro: `crangejoin` reimplements `rangejoin`, written by Robert Picard. Its syntax, interval specification, and output follow `rangejoin`. `rangejoin` itself requires `rangestat`, written by Robert Picard, Nicholas J. Cox, and Roberto Ferrer.

commands.intro: `cpsmatch` reimplements `psmatch2`, written by Edwin Leuven and Barbara Sianesi. Its syntax, options, output, generated variables, and stored results follow `psmatch2`.
later: Until November 16, 2026, SSC distributed `psmatch2` 4.0.12 (January 30, 2016), and ctools 1.3.0 and earlier follow that version. Version 4.1.0 matches the same observations and reports the same effects with different standard errors. The default ATT standard error uses the outcome variance of every control on support, `ate` has ATU and ATE standard errors without `ai()`, and `ai()` reports the population variance unless `samplevar` is specified and corrects for an estimated propensity score. In 4.0.12, `ai()` reported the sample variance unless `population` was specified. `which psmatch2` shows the version on your machine, and `ssc install psmatch2, replace` installs 4.1.0.
references: Leuven, E., and B. Sianesi. 2003. PSMATCH2: Stata module to perform full Mahalanobis and propensity score matching, common support graphing, and covariate imbalance testing. Statistical Software Components S432001, Boston College Department of Economics.

commands.intro: `csort` replaces `sort`, an official Stata command, and uses its syntax.
`cmerge` reimplements `merge`, an official Stata command. Its syntax, options, `_merge` variable, result table, and messages follow `merge`.
`cjoinby` reimplements `joinby`, an official Stata command. Its syntax, options, `_merge` variable, value label, and messages follow `joinby`.

`creshape` reimplements `reshape`, an official Stata command. Its syntax, options, messages, summary table, and the characteristics it records with the data follow `reshape`. The subcommands that only declare, show or clear the settings (`creshape i`, `j`, `xij`, `xi`, `query`, `clear`), and `creshape error`, are carried out by `reshape` itself.
credits: The Stata manual acknowledges that this version of `reshape` was based in part on the work of Jeroen Weesie of Utrecht University (see **[D] reshape**).
references: Weesie, J. 1997. dm48: An enhancement of reshape. *Stata Technical Bulletin* 38: 2-4. Reprinted in *Stata Technical Bulletin Reprints*, vol. 7, pp. 40-43. College Station, TX: Stata Press.

commands.intro: `cfuzzyjoin` reimplements three community commands: `reclink`, written by Michael Blasnik, as `cfuzzyjoin link`; `matchit`, written by Julio D. Raffo (World Intellectual Property Organization), as `cfuzzyjoin match`; and `strgroup`, written by Julian Reif (University of Illinois), as `cfuzzyjoin group`. The syntax, options, scores, results, and messages of each subcommand follow its original.
later: Julian Reif's GitHub repository (github.com/reifjulian/strgroup) has a newer `strgroup`, 1.0.5 (January 2026), with a faster plugin; SSC distributes 1.0.4, which `cfuzzyjoin group` follows.
credits: `matchit` computes gram frequencies with `freqindex` 1.3.1 (April 2019), also by Julio D. Raffo and distributed on SSC (`ssc install freqindex`); `cfuzzyjoin match` follows its similarity functions too.

`strgroup`'s plugin computes the Levenshtein distance with code adapted from David Necas's python-Levenshtein module. `cfuzzyjoin group` computes the same distance with the bit-parallel algorithm of Myers (1999), in the form Hyyrö (2003) gives for the distance between whole strings, and a banded dynamic program (Ukkonen 1985) beyond 64 bytes.
references: Blasnik, M. 2007. RECLINK: Stata module to probabilistically match records. Statistical Software Components S456876, Boston College Department of Economics. Revised January 18, 2010.
Raffo, J. 2015. MATCHIT: Stata module to match two datasets based on similar text patterns. Statistical Software Components S457992, Boston College Department of Economics. Revised May 20, 2020.
Raffo, J., and S. Lhuillery. 2009. How to play the "Names Game": Patent retrieval comparing different heuristics. *Research Policy* 38(10): 1617-1627.

Reif, J. 2010. STRGROUP: Stata module to match strings based on their Levenshtein edit distance. Statistical Software Components S457151, Boston College Department of Economics. Revised August 22, 2023.
Myers, G. 1999. A fast bit-vector algorithm for approximate string matching based on dynamic programming. *Journal of the ACM* 46(3): 395-415.
Hyyrö, H. 2003. A bit-vector algorithm for computing Levenshtein and Damerau edit distances. *Nordic Journal of Computing* 10(1): 29-39.
Ukkonen, E. 1985. Algorithms for approximate string matching. *Information and Control* 64(1-3): 100-118.

commands.intro: `cexport` reimplements Stata's official `export` commands: `export delimited`, `export excel`, `export dbase`, `export spss`, `export sasxport5`, `export sasxport8`, and `export shp`.
`ccollapse` reimplements `collapse`, an official Stata command. Its syntax, statistics, weights, storage types, labels, messages, and return codes follow `collapse`.
credits: In this Stata release `collapse.ado` passes its arguments to `collapse_17.ado` (version 1.1.0, August 17, 2022), which computes the statistics with functions built into Stata. `ccollapse` follows the results of that implementation. The definitions of the percentiles are those of `summarize, detail` and `_pctile`.

commands.intro: `csample` reimplements `sample`, an official Stata command.
`cbsample` reimplements `bsample`, an official Stata command.

`cegen` reimplements `egen`, an official Stata command, and the `egen` functions that ship with Stata. Its syntax, functions, options, storage types, labels, and messages follow `egen`. The `threads()` and `verbose` options are additions in ctools.
credits: Several `egen` functions began as contributions by Stata users, and their files in Stata say so: `anyvalue()`, `mad()`, and `mdev()` are based on programs by Nicholas J. Cox (*Stata Technical Bulletin* 50, insert dm70), and `mtr()` is an update of a program by Timothy J. Schmidt (*Stata Technical Bulletin* 22, insert sss1.1). The Acknowledgments of [D] egen in the Stata manuals also credit David Clayton and Michael Hills with `cut()` and Nicholas J. Cox with many of the other functions.
`cegen` does not copy the tax tables of `mtr()` and does not reimplement functions that ship outside Stata, such as those of `egenmore`: it passes these calls to `egen` itself.
references: Cox, N. J. 1999. dm70: Extensions to generate, extended. *Stata Technical Bulletin* 50: 9-17.
Schmidt, T. J. 1994. sss1.1: Updated U.S. marginal income tax rate function. *Stata Technical Bulletin* 22: 29.

commands.intro: `cencode` reimplements `encode`, an official Stata command. Encoding several variables at once and the `replace` option are additions in ctools.
`cdecode` reimplements `decode`, an official Stata command. Decoding several variables at once and the `replace` option are additions in ctools.

`cqreg` replaces `qreg`, an official Stata command, and uses its syntax, options, output, and stored results. The solver, clustered standard errors, and check for non-unique solutions are implemented in ctools, based on the references in its help file.

new_commands.intro: `csql` is a ctools command, not a reimplementation of a Stata command. Its queries run in [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org), developed by Mark Raasveldt, Hannes Mühleisen, and the DuckDB contributors, and released by the DuckDB Foundation under the MIT license.

uses.name: DuckDB
uses.authors: Mark Raasveldt, Hannes Mühleisen, and the DuckDB contributors

credits: ctools ships DuckDB's C API header (`duckdb.h`). The library itself is not part of ctools: `csql, install` downloads it from DuckDB's own releases, and `library()` loads another DuckDB release (1.1 or later). [help ctools_licenses](help:ctools_licenses) reproduces the DuckDB license.
references: Raasveldt, M., and H. Mühleisen. 2019. DuckDB: An embeddable analytical database. In *Proceedings of the 2019 International Conference on Management of Data (SIGMOD '19)*, 1981-1984. New York: ACM. [https://doi.org/10.1145/3299869.3320212](https://doi.org/10.1145/3299869.3320212).

algorithms: Michael Axtmann, Sascha Witt, Daniel Ferizovic, and Peter Sanders for the In-place Parallel Super Scalar Samplesort ([IPS4o](https://github.com/SaschaWitt/ips4o)) algorithm used in `csort`.
Sergio Correia for [ftools](https://github.com/sergiocorreia/ftools) and Mauricio Caceres Bravo for [gtools](https://github.com/mcaceresb/gtools).
The authors of the libraries compiled into the ctools plugins, listed in `help ctools_licenses`.
